title: TitanSeal sealants launch: derive a single-color logo system from one supplied mark, neutralize a mixed-light jobsite capture set to an in-frame grey card, and data-merge one press-ready SKU label per row plus the single-color cartons
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork product-packaging brief (a Gulf B2B trading firm launching its first private-label industrial-sealants line: approved master logo to be extended into a variant system, swappable per-SKU cartridge/tube labels and single-color shipping cartons built as data-driven templates, plus a digital asset pack) and laundered to a fictional coined brand, 'TitanSeal' — no real company, product, person, or trademark is named; the delivery channels referenced (an online marketplace listing, a messaging catalog card, social/web tiles, an email signature) are generic formats, not the client. REPOSITIONED for connector reality on four counts: (1) the label 'swappable-element template' is only connector-doable as a genuinely hand-authored InDesign data-merge document (.indd carrying live <<fields>> AND an @-prefixed image column) — NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (fields would not bind) and NOT a multi-record grid (document_merge_data_layout emits exactly one file per row), so the client supplies the authored .indd and the merge produces one single-record label per SKU. (2) The carton 'template' is a hand-authored Illustrator Variables .ai, but document_merge_data_vector is TEXT-ONLY — it cannot bind an image column — so the mono mark is PRE-PLACED once in the authored carton art and only the text variables (SKU name/code/pack-count/carton-size/batch) repopulate per row. (3) The logo VARIANTS are DERIVED from the one supplied mark by real raster/vector ops (isolate-to-transparency → prep → vectorize for the clean brand SVG; select→vectorize for the single-color silhouette marks), never redrawn; and because image_remove_background isolates only the OUTER ground and cannot punch open a letter's enclosed counter, a clean white wordmark knockout for a DARK ground is NOT connector-doable — so the reversed/dark-ground variant is delivered as the OPEN-COUNTER droplet-icon silhouette only, a deliberate constraint-reasoning beat, while the full-wordmark single-color mark is scoped to light grounds. (4) The 'jobsite hero' is repositioned from a single stock license to a client-supplied SET of jobsite captures shot across one day under deliberately mismatched light, each carrying an 18% grey card in frame, so the digital pack becomes a gradeable cross-asset neutralization rather than one auto-toned photo. Authoring the multi-page brand-standards PDF body copy/typography and any from-scratch page composition remain OUT OF SCOPE for the connector and are flagged as human/desktop finishing.
one_line_ask: From one supplied TitanSeal master logo derive the clean brand SVG plus the single-color marks and the wide lockup by real raster/vector ops (deciding the correct prep-and-trace order and the single-color path yourself); neutralize a set of mixed-light jobsite captures to the grey card each one carries so they read as one matched set and size the platform tiles; then data-merge the client's authored InDesign label template against the SKU roster into one press-ready label per row and text-merge the single-color cartons, exporting the print PDFs and the digital pack.
full_brief:
TitanSeal is a Gulf-based B2B private-label industrial-sealants brand launching three SKUs. The master logo is approved and supplied to you as one high-resolution PNG on a solid white ground (the wordmark 'TitanSeal' with a solid caulk-bead droplet icon, in deep industrial blue). The client also supplies two genuinely desktop-authored print mechanicals carrying real merge fields/variables — a hand-built InDesign wrap-label template and a hand-built Illustrator carton template — a SKU roster as a CSV, and a folder of jobsite photographs the field team shot for the launch. Using ONLY the Adobe connector, deliver four things.

FIRST, the LOGO SYSTEM, derived from the one supplied mark (do not redraw it): a clean scalable brand vector; a single-color mark for one-color printing; a reversed treatment for dark and photographic backgrounds; and a wide horizontal lockup band for banners and email. The supplied file sits on a solid white ground, so think about the order of operations — a mark still carrying its white field will trace or recolor as a white-bounded block. Note also that our droplet icon is a solid open shape but the wordmark letters have enclosed counters; if a clean one-color reversed wordmark for a dark ground is not achievable with these tools, deliver the reversed treatment from the icon instead and tell us why, rather than shipping a wordmark with filled-in letter holes.

SECOND, the DIGITAL PACK. We are NOT reshooting. The jobsite folder was shot across a single day under whatever light was there — cold overcast outside, warm tungsten in a fit-out corner, greenish strip-lighting in a bay, golden late sun — and a couple of frames are tilted and one is dark, so straight out of the folder they look like a mismatched jumble and a launch feed of mismatched shots reads cheap. To make consistency checkable we laid an 18% grey card into a corner of every frame. Bring the whole set to one consistent, true-to-material look by neutralizing each frame to the grey card it contains (the card must read as clean neutral grey, equal across the channels, in your finished frame) so that once every card is neutral the set shares one white point; hold a subtle cool-industrial house feel in the final look, but do NOT force one blanket correction across the folder — each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure, and tone decision to land on the shared target. Be careful with the frame whose hero subject is a bead of our GREY sealant: grey product under neutral light is not a colour cast — if that frame's card already reads neutral, do not 'warm' or 'cool' it chasing an imagined cast, or you will throw off the very material we are selling. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm the set is matched, not eyeballed. From the matched set, size the platform tiles we need: a 1:1 social tile, a 16:9 web banner, a slim email-signature strip, and a 1:1 messaging-catalog card — each framed on the work, with the grey card cropped OUT of the delivered tile.

THIRD, the LABELS. We have hand-built the InDesign wrap-label template with the real placeholder fields and a logo image frame, and we are giving you the roster; merge them so every SKU gets its own single-page label with its name, code, volume, colorway and barcode bound from the roster and the brand mark dropped into its frame, then hand back one press-ready label PDF covering every SKU (one page per SKU). Bind the copy verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite our codes or volumes.

FOURTH, the CARTONS. We have hand-built the Illustrator carton die-line with named Variables and the mono mark already placed in the art; repopulate the text variables from the roster for the 20-cartridge and 24-tube packs and export the single-color carton artwork to PDF with the die-line preserved.

Acceptance: every grey card neutral (channel spread within a hair of zero) and the whole jobsite set matched to one white point while the grey-sealant frame keeps its true material colour; the logo system derived from the one supplied mark with the correct prep/trace order and an honest reversed treatment; exactly one finished label per roster row; and the single-color carton PDF with its die-line intact. OUT OF SCOPE for the connector (flag as human/desktop finishing): authoring the brand-standards PDF body and typography pages, drawing any new layout from scratch, and the marketplace listing-page composition.

inputs.name: titanseal_master_logo.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A professional industrial-sealants master logo on a SOLID WHITE (non-transparent) background at high resolution (~3000x2400 px): the single word 'TitanSeal' as the large dominant wordmark in a bold condensed geometric sans-serif, deep industrial blue (#0B3D91), with a small SOLID caulk-bead / droplet icon (a filled teardrop shape with no interior hole) to its left, and a small tagline 'INDUSTRIAL SEALANTS' beneath the wordmark. Flat vector-style solid fills only, crisp clean edges, no gradients/shadows, centred with generous white margin all around, horizontal.
inputs.realism_notes: Delivered on a SOLID WHITE ground (as a real approved-logo PNG hand-off often is), NOT pre-cut to transparency — so the agent must isolate the mark to transparency BEFORE any recolor or trace, or a white-bounded block results (dependent-step discipline). Solid flat fills and generous margin so isolate/crop/vectorize and the 3:1 reframe all behave. Two glyph kinds on purpose: the droplet is a SOLID open shape (safe to isolate and reverse for a dark ground) while the wordmark letters carry enclosed counters (which image_remove_background cannot punch open) — this is what forces the honest 'reversed = icon-only for dark grounds' decision. Declared at camera/vector scale so every derivation is downscale-only, never an upscale.
inputs.twist: Two traps ride on this one file: (a) it is on a white ground, so isolate-to-transparency must precede recolor/trace; (b) the wordmark has enclosed counters image_remove_background cannot open, so a clean white wordmark knockout for a DARK ground is not connector-doable and the reversed treatment must fall back to the open-counter droplet icon.

inputs.name: titanseal_label_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD wrap-around cartridge/tube label (approx 200mm x 95mm + 3mm bleed, one SKU per page). It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<SKU_NAME>>, <<SKU_CODE>>, <<VOLUME>>, <<COLORWAY>>, <<BARCODE>>, and ONE @-prefixed image-path merge column, @Logo, wired to a logo image frame plus a static hazard-pictogram zone. Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the brand mark reaches the label ONLY as a merge bind through the @Logo image frame. Built by hand so the fields and the image field actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus a genuine @image-path column, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record label is the correct, connector-doable shape and page-count must equal row-count. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. The @Logo column gives the agent-produced vectorized brand mark a real, connector-doable path onto every label without any free-form placement (mirrors the two-image-column merge pattern used elsewhere in the corpus).

inputs.name: titanseal_carton_template.ai
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built Adobe Illustrator carton die-line (.ai) for a single-color (black) corrugated shipping carton, authored with named Illustrator Variables (text/visibility) bound to columns SKU_NAME, SKU_CODE, PACK_COUNT, CARTON_SIZE, BATCH so the TEXT repopulates per row. The mono brand mark and the fragile/this-way-up pictograms are drawn into the art ONCE as static vector — they are NOT variables — because document_merge_data_vector is text-only and cannot bind an image. Includes the die-line for both the 20-cartridge and 24-tube size variants.
inputs.realism_notes: AUTHORED [T] Illustrator Variables template supplied by the client. Single-color black to match the brief's cost constraint. Only TEXT variables merge — document_merge_data_vector cannot bind an image column — so the mark is pre-placed static art, not a per-row image bind. Variables must be pre-defined in the .ai so the vector merge can bind the CSV text columns.

inputs.name: titanseal_sku_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV whose header is SKU_NAME,SKU_CODE,VOLUME,COLORWAY,BARCODE,PACK_COUNT,CARTON_SIZE,BATCH,@Logo and which has exactly 3 data rows: 'MS Polymer Sealant',TS-MS600-GRY,600ml,Grey,6291100000017,20,20-cartridge,B2701,@titanseal_logo.svg; 'PU Construction Sealant',TS-PU600-GRY,600ml,Grey,6291100000024,20,20-cartridge,B2701,@titanseal_logo.svg; 'Neutral Silicone Sealant',TS-NS300-WHT,300ml,White,6291100000031,24,24-tube,B2701,@titanseal_logo.svg. The @Logo column carries the SAME vectorized brand mark file in every row so the label merge drops the one shared mark onto every SKU's label as a merge bind. Header names must exactly match the .indd <<fields>> and the .ai Variables.
inputs.realism_notes: Plausible EAN-13 barcodes and the three exact SKUs from the brief. Column names are the binding contract with BOTH authored templates — they must match exactly or the merge fails. The label merge reads <<SKU_NAME/SKU_CODE/VOLUME/COLORWAY/BARCODE>> + @Logo; the carton vector merge reads only the TEXT columns SKU_NAME/SKU_CODE/PACK_COUNT/CARTON_SIZE/BATCH (it ignores @Logo, being text-only). Three rows => the label merge must produce exactly three label pages.

inputs.name: capture_01.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera capture (~4500 px long edge) of a jobsite detail: a gloved hand running a bead of grey sealant along an exterior aluminium window frame, shot under COLD OVERCAST daylight (distinct cool bluish cast), frame tilted ~4 deg, an 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame, real skin pores and glove weave and frame dust, shallow depth of field, documentary not staged, clean negative space to one side for later cropping, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool-cast, TILTED frame — needs straighten then a warming neutralization to its card. Camera-scale (~4500 px) so every platform crop is downscale-only. Neutral filename (capture_01) so the treatment is not telegraphed; which frames are tilted/warm/cool/the trap lives only in these notes and the step notes.

inputs.name: capture_02.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4500 px long edge) of an interior fit-out corner: a sealed skirting/joint detail lit by WARM TUNGSTEN work-lamps (distinct warm orange cast), frame level, an 18% grey card in one corner, real material texture and dust, documentary, negative space to one side, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Warm-cast, LEVEL frame — must move the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames (cool it) to neutralize its card to the shared white point. No straighten needed. Neutral filename.

inputs.name: capture_03.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4500 px long edge) whose hero is a fresh bead of GENUINELY GREY sealant tooled along a concrete-to-metal joint, shot under NEAR-NEUTRAL balanced light (no strong cast), frame level, an 18% grey card in one corner, real crumb/grit/tooling-mark texture, documentary, negative space to one side, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP FRAME. The hero material is truly grey and the light is near-neutral, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. Correct move: essentially NO white-balance shift (match exposure/brightness to the set only). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' move used on frames 1/x, or 'cools an imagined cast', will push the card off-neutral and tint the grey product — the exact material being sold. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Level frame, no straighten. Neutral filename — nothing here says it is the trap.

inputs.name: capture_04.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4500 px long edge) of a scaffold/facade sealant detail in OPEN SHADE (strong cool blue shade cast), frame tilted ~3 deg, an 18% grey card in one corner, real texture, documentary, negative space to one side, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Strong cool shade cast, TILTED — straighten then a firm warming neutralization; a stronger correction than frame 1. Neutral filename.

inputs.name: capture_05.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4500 px long edge) of a sealed expansion joint under MIDDAY DIRECT SUN (near-neutral, slightly warm, bright), frame level, an 18% grey card in one corner, hard shadows and real texture, documentary, wide clean negative space to one side (intended as the web-banner source), no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Near-neutral bright frame — a small WB nudge only, plus highlight control against the bright sun; over-correcting pushes it off the set. Level. Wide negative space so the 16:9 banner crop lands. Neutral filename.

inputs.name: capture_06.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4500 px long edge) of an indoor bay sealant application under GREENISH FLUORESCENT strip-lighting (distinct green-cyan cast), frame tilted ~4 deg, an 18% grey card in one corner, real texture, documentary, negative space to one side, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Green-cyan fluorescent cast, TILTED — straighten then neutralize with BOTH a temperature and a tint (magenta) move to kill the green, distinct from the pure warm/cool frames. Neutral filename.
inputs.twist: The fluorescent cast is green-magenta, not blue-amber — a temperature-only correction leaves it green; the frame needs a tint move too, so a one-axis 'warm/cool' habit fails here.

inputs.name: capture_07.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4500 px long edge) of an exterior sealed cladding seam under STRONG GOLDEN LATE-AFTERNOON SUN (heavy warm cast), frame level, an 18% grey card in one corner, long warm shadows and real texture, documentary, negative space to one side (intended as a 1:1 card source), no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Heavy warm golden cast, LEVEL — a firm cooling neutralization to the shared white point, opposite the cool frames. Level. Neutral filename.

inputs.name: capture_08.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4500 px long edge) of a dim service riser sealant detail lit by a single work lamp (mixed warm + ambient, UNDEREXPOSED), frame tilted ~3 deg, an 18% grey card in one corner, real texture and noise, documentary, negative space to one side, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Underexposed and mixed-light, TILTED — straighten, then the dominant move is TONAL (lift exposure/shadows, control noise) before neutralizing the card to the shared white point; a different problem class from the pure cast frames. Neutral filename.

outputs.name: titanseal_logo_transparent.png
outputs.spec: The supplied master mark isolated to a transparent ground (outer white field removed) at full resolution — the foundation asset every downstream derivation and lockup is built from; delivered as a brand-kit placement asset for light grounds.

outputs.name: titanseal_logo.svg
outputs.spec: Clean scalable colour SVG of the full mark, traced ONLY after the mark is isolated to transparency and cropped to its bounds (prep-before-trace) — razor-sharp at any lockup size, no captured white field. This is the vector bound into every label via the roster @Logo column.

outputs.name: titanseal_mark_mono_black.svg
outputs.spec: Single-color BLACK silhouette of the full mark for one-color printing on LIGHT grounds, produced by selecting the mark and vectorizing it (a selection fed to image_vectorize returns a solid black silhouette). Scoped to light grounds because the enclosed wordmark counters cannot be punched open by the connector.

outputs.name: titanseal_icon_reversed.svg
outputs.spec: Reversed/dark-ground treatment delivered as the OPEN-COUNTER droplet ICON silhouette only (selected via prompt, then vectorized), because a clean one-color WORDMARK knockout for a dark ground is not connector-doable (image_remove_background cannot open the letters' enclosed counters). A vector silhouette whose fill is set white at placement, usable at any size on dark/photographic backgrounds.

outputs.name: titanseal_horizontal_lockup.png
outputs.spec: 3:1 horizontal-lockup band cropped/reframed from the isolated transparent master (a horizontal band of the source, downscale-only, no invented pixels), centered on the mark; the top/bottom transparent margin is cropped to hit the ratio. For web banner / email use.

outputs.name: titanseal_labels_merged.pdf
outputs.spec: Press-ready PDF, exactly one page per SKU (page-count = roster row-count = 3), from the authored .indd + roster data-merge; each label binds <<SKU_NAME/SKU_CODE/VOLUME/COLORWAY/BARCODE>> verbatim from the roster and drops the vectorized brand mark into its logo frame via the @Logo column (merge bind, never free-form placement); 3mm bleed.

outputs.name: titanseal_cartons_merged.pdf
outputs.spec: Single-color black carton artwork PDF for the 20-cartridge and 24-tube packs, from the authored .ai Variables + roster TEXT-merge (SKU_NAME/SKU_CODE/PACK_COUNT/CARTON_SIZE/BATCH); the mono mark and pictograms are the template's static art (vector merge is text-only); die-line preserved.

outputs.name: jobsite_matched_set_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized, straightened jobsite captures delivered as the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked): each card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero), the whole set is matched to one shared white point while holding a subtle cool-industrial house tone, and the grey-sealant frame (capture_03) keeps its true material colour (its card held neutral, not tinted). Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame.

outputs.name: titanseal_social_tile_1080.png
outputs.spec: 1080x1080 social tile cropped from one neutralized master, framed on the work with the grey card cropped OUT (card-exclusion checked here, never card-neutrality).

outputs.name: titanseal_web_banner_1920x1080.png
outputs.spec: 1920x1080 web banner cropped from a wide neutralized master, grey card cropped OUT, downscale-only from the ~4500px source.

outputs.name: titanseal_email_signature_350x120.png
outputs.spec: 350x120 email-signature strip cropped from a neutralized master, grey card cropped OUT.

outputs.name: titanseal_whatsapp_card_1x1.png
outputs.spec: 1:1 messaging-catalog product card cropped from a neutralized master, grey card cropped OUT.

connector_workflow.note: Initialize upload of the client's approved master logo PNG into the project workspace.
Finalize the logo upload to get a stable asset URL for the derivation chain.

DEPENDENT-STEP GATE: the supplied mark sits on a SOLID WHITE ground, so isolate it to transparency FIRST — every later recolor/trace depends on this. Skipping it (tracing or recoloring the raw white-ground file) yields a white-bounded block. remove_background isolates the OUTER white field only; the wordmark's enclosed letter counters remain filled with the captured white (fine on light grounds, they read white) — which is why the dark-ground reversed variant must fall back to the open-counter icon (steps 8-9). Output → transparency (NOT select→invert→fill).
Prep-before-trace: crop the isolated mark to its tight bounds so image_vectorize traces only the mark, not the transparent field/margin.

Trace the prepared (isolated, cropped) raster into a clean scalable COLOUR SVG for lockups — no redrawing. This vector is the mark bound into every label via @Logo. Tracing the raw white-ground file instead would bake in a white rectangle bound — the trap this prep order avoids.
Select the mark as the subject on the isolated master, to feed a selection (not the raw raster) into vectorize for the single-color silhouette.

A SELECTION fed to image_vectorize returns a solid BLACK silhouette — that is exactly the single-color mono mark wanted for one-color printing on light grounds. (This documented selection→silhouette behavior is the correct single-color path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image with no opacity and image_apply_monochromatic_tint yields a tonal tint, not a flat single color — neither gives a clean single-color mark, so both are deliberately avoided.)

Semantically select only the caulk-bead droplet icon ('the solid teardrop droplet icon'). The droplet is a SOLID OPEN shape with no enclosed counter, so it can be reversed cleanly for a dark ground — unlike the wordmark, whose letter counters image_remove_background cannot punch open. A named-part selection, not a hue/region.

Vectorize the icon selection into the open-counter droplet silhouette — the honest reversed/dark-ground treatment (its SVG fill is set white at placement). Delivering a full-wordmark 'white knockout' here would ship letters with filled-in counters on a dark ground; the constraint-correct answer is the icon, and the agent must reason to it.

Reframe the isolated transparent master to a 3:1 horizontal-lockup band by cropping (downscale-only, output never larger than the source, no invented pixels), centered on the mark so the icon+wordmark stay in the band; the top/bottom transparent margin is cropped away to hit 3:1. onSubjectClipping='extract'.
Triage: this frame is tilted ~4 deg — level it first. (Only the tilted frames 01/04/06/08 get straightened; deciding which is part of the job.)

Cool overcast cast: WARM it (positive temperature) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey and hold a subtle cool-industrial house tone. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card — do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces any deprecated color_temperature/vibrance calls).

Level frame, warm tungsten cast: move OPPOSITE the cool frames — COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and it matches the shared white point set on frame 01. Distinct numbers from frame 01. Report the move.

THE TRAP FRAME. The hero bead is genuinely GREY and the light is near-neutral, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. Correct move: essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction, or 'cools an imagined cast', neutralizes the card off-neutral and tints the grey product being sold. Decision driven by THIS card, not the batch. Level frame, no straighten. Report that WB was held.
Tilted ~3 deg under strong cool shade — level it.
Strong cool blue shade cast: a FIRMER warming correction than frame 01 to bring its card to neutral and onto the shared white point. Adaptive — the magnitude differs per frame. Report the move.

Near-neutral bright midday frame: only a SMALL WB nudge to land its card on the shared white point, plus highlight recovery against the hard sun; over-correcting pushes it off the set. Level. Report the (small) move. This wide frame is the web-banner source.
Tilted ~4 deg under greenish fluorescent — level it.

Green-cyan fluorescent cast: this needs BOTH a temperature AND a tint (toward magenta) move to neutralize the card — a temperature-only 'warm/cool' habit leaves it green. Two-axis correction distinct from every other frame. Report the move.

Heavy warm golden late-sun cast, level: a FIRM cooling correction until its card reads neutral and matches the shared white point — opposite direction and larger magnitude than the cool frames. Report the move. This frame is a 1:1 card source.
Tilted ~3 deg, dim/underexposed — level it.

Underexposed mixed light: the DOMINANT move is TONAL (lift exposure/shadows, control noise/clarity), THEN neutralize its card to the shared white point — a different problem class from the pure-cast frames, so blanket batch numbers fail. Report the move. Frames 01-08 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.

Crop a neutralized master to the 1080x1080 social tile, framing on the work with the grey card cropped OUT (card-exclusion checked here; neutrality is graded on the retained cap01_neutralized master, not on this crop). Downscale-only from ~4500px, onSubjectClipping='extract'.
Crop the wide midday master to the 1920x1080 web banner, grey card cropped OUT, downscale-only from ~4500px. onSubjectClipping='extract'.
Crop a neutralized master to the 350x120 email-signature strip, grey card cropped OUT, downscale-only. onSubjectClipping='extract'.
Crop a neutralized master to a 1:1 messaging-catalog card, grey card cropped OUT, downscale-only. onSubjectClipping='extract'.

Initialize upload of the client-authored InDesign label template, the roster CSV, and the agent-produced vectorized brand mark (titanseal_logo.svg) so the merge can resolve the @Logo column. Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references.
Finalize the label upload; returns the asset URNs the template and the roster's @Logo column resolve to.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the 3 roster rows (<<SKU_NAME/SKU_CODE/VOLUME/COLORWAY/BARCODE>>) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live fields AND resolve the @Logo image column (the vectorized mark, same SVG every row) into the label's logo frame — producing EXACTLY ONE label per row (3 labels). The mark reaches the label only through this image-column bind; free-form placement is banned. [T] requires the hand-authored template. A convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-record grid would not bind/produce and is NOT used.

Export the merged label document to a press-ready PDF with 3mm bleed. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all 3 labels, one page per SKU) in one call — no per-record named export. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 3; fewer means the merge collapsed rows and failed.
Initialize upload of the client-authored Illustrator carton die-line with named Variables and the mono mark already placed as static art.
Finalize the carton upload to get the asset URN for the vector merge.

TEXT-ONLY Illustrator Variables merge: bind the roster TEXT columns (SKU_NAME/SKU_CODE/PACK_COUNT/CARTON_SIZE/BATCH) into the authored .ai's named Variables for the 20-cartridge and 24-tube packs. document_merge_data_vector CANNOT bind an image, so the mono mark/pictograms stay as the template's static art — the @Logo column is ignored here by design.
Export the merged carton .ai to a press-ready single-color black PDF, die-line preserved.

chaining_note: Strict output→input chaining throughout, in four dependent sub-chains. LOGO SYSTEM: the master logo is uploaded (1→2) into logo_asset, isolated to transparency by image_remove_background (3) — the dependent-step gate every derivation hangs on — then that transparent master fans out: crop_to_bounds (4) → vectorize → clean colour SVG (5); select_subject (6) → vectorize → single-color black silhouette (7); select_by_prompt the droplet (8) → vectorize → open-counter reversed icon (9); and crop_and_resize → 3:1 lockup (10). DIGITAL PACK: eight jobsite captures each run a per-frame grade — image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 01/04/06/08 (11,15,18,21), then image_apply_adjustments neutralizes each frame to its own in-frame grey card (12,13,14,16,17,19,20,22), every one a different reasoned decision (warm the cool/shade frames, cool the tungsten/golden frames, a two-axis temperature+tint move on the fluorescent frame, a tonal-first lift on the underexposed frame, and WB HELD on the genuinely-grey trap frame 03) so all eight converge on one shared white point; four of the neutralized masters are then cropped to the platform tiles (23-26) with the grey card cropped out. LABELS: the authored .indd, the roster CSV and the agent-produced titanseal_logo.svg are uploaded (27→28) and consumed by document_merge_data_layout (29), whose merged .indd is exported by document_render_layout (30) to the one-page-per-SKU label PDF. CARTONS: the authored .ai is uploaded (31→32) and text-merged by document_merge_data_vector (33), whose merged .ai is exported by document_render_vector (34). Every step after the initial uploads consumes a prior step's output; the deliverable package emerges entirely from the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 34 connector calls, 14 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (asset storage, image raster/vector, document layout/vector merge+render), above the ≥10 call / ≥6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 3 upload init/finalize pairs and the auto-straighten auto-ops. The core is not a repeated recipe: (1) the logo system is a chain of DEPENDENT decisions — isolate-to-transparency must precede every recolor/trace, prep-before-trace must precede vectorize, and the single-color path is a reasoned choice (selection→silhouette, not color_overlay/monochromatic_tint) capped by a genuine constraint-reasoning beat (the enclosed-counter limit forces the reversed variant to the open-counter icon); (2) the eight-frame jobsite grade is eight DIFFERENT reasoned corrections (warm, cool, two-axis green-magenta, tonal-first, and WB-held on the grey trap) all forced to converge on one measurable target, the in-frame 18% grey card, so a blanket batch correction cannot pass; (3) two authored-template data-merges — a one-file-per-row InDesign label merge binding the agent-produced vector mark through an @-image column, and a TEXT-ONLY Illustrator Variables carton merge where the agent must know the image cannot bind and the mark stays static art. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling (all sources declared at camera/vector scale, all crops downscale-only), no from-scratch layout, no convert_pdf_to_indd (both templates are supplied authored files), image_crop_and_resize pinned to onSubjectClipping='extract', and deprecated tone tools replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): three independent gates the agent can actually trip. (a) The eight jobsite captures each carry a physical 18% grey card and must each be neutralized to it so the set shares one white point — the trap is capture_03, whose hero is a genuinely GREY sealant under near-neutral light so its card is ALREADY neutral; a naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction (or cools an imagined cast) tints the grey product being sold, and the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance; the agent must REPORT the final WB/exposure move per frame so 'matched' is verifiable, not asserted. (b) The logo system's dependent order — a mark still on its white ground will trace/recolor as a white-bounded block, so isolate-to-transparency must come first; and because image_remove_background cannot punch open the wordmark's enclosed counters, a clean white WORDMARK knockout for a dark ground is not achievable, so the constraint-correct reversed deliverable is the open-counter droplet ICON, which the agent must reason to rather than shipping filled-in letters. (c) The label merge must bind into the supplied authored .indd (a convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-record grid fails), producing page-count = row-count = 3. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit frames to a common measurable white point each needing its own opposite-direction (and sometimes two-axis) correction; constraint-reasoning around the remove_background enclosed-counter limit and the vector-merge text-only limit; and prep-before-trace discipline (isolate→crop-to-bounds→vectorize; selection→silhouette). TRAP: the grey-sealant frame that must NOT be 'corrected', and the merge trap where only the authored single-record .indd binds. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, never an agent pixel-readout): grey card neutral (per-channel spread near zero) and one shared white point evaluated on the eight RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (card in frame), with card-EXCLUSION checked separately on the four delivered tiles (card cropped out); the agent's reported per-frame WB/exposure params; the logo SVG clean and white-field-free; the reversed deliverable the open-counter icon; exactly one label page per roster row (=3); and the single-color carton PDF with die-line intact.
